stocks.note: Numbers as of market close April 24th.
stocks.news:
Tech kept the bid Friday. Intel (INTC +23.64%) ripped after finally posting a clean quarter (Q1 EPS $0.29, revenue $13.58B) with both client and data center beating estimates. Reminder: the U.S. Government still owns a 10% stake from August 2025.

Meanwhile Google (GOOG +1.35%) cut a $40B check to Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude. Google Cloud already hosts Anthropic's work and supplies its training chips. The takeaway: AI capex is not slowing.

Markets trade as usual this week with the Fed announcement on Wednesday.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET April 26th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year sat dead flat into the weekend. Powell-case-closed news removed one tail risk on Fed independence. Wednesday's rate decision is now the only thing the bond market is watching.

Gold pulled back slightly off record highs, the first breather in a multi-week run.

WTI climbed back over $96 as airlines worldwide continue rerouting around the Middle East and canceling routes outright. Asia-Pacific and European carriers are taking the biggest hit. Expect summer fare hikes and fewer seats, and watch oil for any rate-cut ripple effects.

crypto.note: Numbers as of 4:00 PM ET on April 26th.
crypto.commentary:
Saylor passed BlackRock. Strategy (MSTR -0.84%) now holds about 815,061 BTC, more than BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF (IBIT). Out of roughly 20 million Bitcoin in existence, one founder controls over 4% of supply, and he's been buying since 2020 through every crash.

On the regulatory front, Wisconsin sued Kalshi and Polymarket for running unlicensed gambling, the latest move in the state-by-state fight over whether prediction markets are gambling or regulated financial products. Worth watching as this category explodes.

real_estate.homebuilder: Zillow Cuts 2026 Forecast to +0.5%; Buyers Officially Take the Wheel
real_estate.commentary:
The DOJ dropping its case against Powell on Friday clears the runway for Kevin Warsh as next Fed Chair, and Wednesday's rate decision lands with consumer confidence at an all-time low (Univ. Of Michigan). Translation for sellers: pressure on the Fed to cut is building, and Zillow's "sub-6% mortgage" trigger for a real housing reset is finally inside the strike zone.

Zillow just cut its 2026 housing call to 0.5% existing-home sales growth, citing rate lock-in and flat prices. They flagged what we're already seeing locally:

• Inventory: highest since 2020.
• Days on market: climbing.
• Price cuts and seller concessions: both up.

Total active inventory across the 15-city board is 2,802 with 274 fresh listings today.

For listing agents this week: Price to today's market, not last year's. Wednesday's Fed decision is binary. Either rates dip and you ride a brief showing wave, or they hold and inventory keeps stacking. Either way, the "list high and wait" seller is the one taking price cuts in May.
